prompt: Some people say that in the digital age, theatres and cinemas are no longer important as people can watch all the entertainment they want online. Others argue that theatres and cinemas are still important both economically and culturally. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Online platforms have changed the way people watch films and performances. Some therefore believe that theatres and cinemas are no longer necessary, while others argue that they still have economic and cultural value. Although online entertainment is convenient, I believe these venues remain important because they offer a unique experience and support local economies.

On the one hand, online entertainment has advantages. Streaming services allow people to watch films, concerts and plays whenever and wherever they want. This is usually cheaper than buying tickets, travelling to a venue and paying for parking or food. It also helps those who live far from cities or cannot travel easily. For example, a family can watch a new film at home without buying several cinema tickets. Therefore, many people consider traditional venues unnecessary.

On the other hand, theatres and cinemas offer benefits that online platforms cannot replace. A large screen and high-quality sound make films more enjoyable, while live performances create a direct connection between actors and the audience. These venues also provide jobs and attract customers to nearby cafés and restaurants. Moreover, theatres preserve local stories, languages and traditions by presenting them to new generations. For example, a historical play can help young people understand their cultural background. For these reasons, I believe these places still play an essential role.

In conclusion, online services make entertainment cheaper and easier to access. However, theatres and cinemas support the economy, protect culture and offer a special shared experience. In my opinion, they should continue to exist alongside online platforms.
